طَعْنَةٌ سُلْكَى [A thrust, or piercing thrust,] directed right towards the face. (S, K.) And أَرٌ سُلْكَى [An affair] rightly directed; (K, TA;) and so رَأْىٌ [an opinion]: (TA:) or the former, [an affair] following one uniform course. (ISk, TA.) ―
-b2- In the saying of Keys Ibn-'Eyzárah, “غَدَاةَ تَنَادَوْا ثُمَّ قَامُوا فَأَجْمَعُوا
بِقَتْلِىَ سُلْكَى لَيْسَ فِيهَا تَنَازُعُ
” he means [In the morning when they congregated, then arose and determined upon my slaughter] with a strong resolution in respect of which there was no contention. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
